channel.description: Latest articles from Potomac Local News (potomaclocal.com)

item.title: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules
item.description: Manassas City Council approved a first reading of a zoning ordinance that tightens development rules for data centers and other large industrial projects, citing noise, appearance, and proximity concerns near residential areas.

item.title: Prince William Debuts Senior Pop-Up Program
item.description: Prince William County is launching its Seniors Without Walls program in February 2026, using pop-up events as an interim step toward a future senior center.

item.title: Fredericksburg Region Adopts First Economic Strategy
item.description: Leaders in the Fredericksburg area are moving forward with the region’s first coordinated economic strategy after an 18-month planning effort aimed at tackling congestion, workforce gaps, and long-term growth.

item.title: Osbourn Students Walk Out Over ICE Policies
item.description: More than 3o0 students at Osbourn High School in Manassas walked out of classes Wednesday afternoon to protest federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement policies, school officials and participants said.

item.title: Violent Crime Falls In Prince William
item.description: Prince William County police reported overall crime down about 9.9% and violent crime down about 18% from 2024 to 2025, while pointing to the Crisis Receiving Center’s role in reducing time spent on behavioral health calls.

item.title: Triune Brings ‘Prince Of Egypt’ to Journey Stage
item.description: Triune Entertainment will stage “The Prince of Egypt” over three weekends in March 2026, with evening and matinee performances at Journey Stage in Warrenton.

item.title: Stafford Schools Push Back On Kraken Power Line
item.description: Stafford County School Board members are urging state lawmakers to restore stronger protections for schools as Dominion Energy advances plans for a 500-kilovolt transmission line that would run through the county.

item.title: Council OKs Princess Anne Townhomes
item.description: Fredericksburg City Council unanimously approved a mixed-use infill project on Princess Anne Street that will bring new townhomes, restore a historic gas station, and add a public pedestrian link to the city’s riverfront trail system.

item.title: Major Road Projects Advance in Prince William’s Six-Year Capital Plan
item.description: Prince William County is dedicating the largest share of its proposed $1.56 billion six-year Capital Improvement Program to transportation, with major road projects moving forward and new fiscal strategies aimed at saving taxpayers millions.
